utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay, I think everyone's here. Diego, you made it, good.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Train was late. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: No problem. First thing, the Leeds fire door sign-off. Hedda said the contractor comes Thursday, not Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Thursday works. I'll be on site.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Great. Elif, did the badge reader quote come through?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Um, I think so? Hamid forwarded something. Somewhere around the, the usual range.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: The usual range being what, roughly? I have 2,300 in the budget line.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'd have to look. It was not wildly off, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right. Can you send it to me after this so I can compare against the line?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sure, yes. Today.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Is that the reader for the second floor entrance or the car park side?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Second floor. I think. Maybe both, actually.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Well, that's a big difference in price.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Let's get the quote in front of us first. Okay, moving on. The cleaning contract in Leeds.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, um, so Brightwash is up at the end of this month, and they sent over the renewal terms last week.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right, I've got the email here. Before you go on, they want an answer by the fourteenth, I believe.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Oh, is it the fourteenth? I thought it was the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fourteenth for the rate lock. After that they said the price goes back to list.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Okay. Good to know. That, that changes the timing a bit.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Which option are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Well, so far just the one, really. I think maybe we should just renew them. Two years, six percent up on the current rate, so it comes to forty-four thousand a year.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Forty-four, so that's up from, what, a bit over forty-one?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, about forty-one and a half, I think.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Forty-one five-ish. Okay, six percent of that is, um, about twenty-five hundred. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And that's two years locked at that figure.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they put in the email. Flat for both years.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Hm. Devil's advocate, but what happens in year two if the market drops? We're stuck.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: That's true, I suppose. But I mean, it's not like cleaning rates are going to fall.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: You never know.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: They won't.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Fine, fine. I just like to ask.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Marco, what's the argument for staying put, beyond not having to change anything?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: So, I looked at the complaints log, the one the office team keeps. Over the last twelve months there were only eleven issues, and most were small, like a missed bin.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: And I talked to Joao a bit about what a switch looks like. I think maybe three weeks of disruption, new people learning the floor plan, keys, alarm codes, all that.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Three weeks is a long time though. People complain about everything in the first month.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Right, that's kind of my point.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Eleven in a year is about one a month. That's not nothing but it's not bad.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Seems fine to me.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Eleven could also mean people stopped reporting. Has anybody checked whether staff still use the log?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, I don't know. I think they do. Bilal still sends stuff through.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Bilal's the one who chases the portal. I can ask him.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I'm not saying it's wrong. Just that a quiet log isn't the same as a clean office.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I mean, the big picture is we want something that doesn't need our attention, right? And Brightwash mostly doesn't.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Mostly. Let me look at the contract a second. There's a clause about the supplies, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: There's something about consumables. I think they bill those on top?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Section four, yes. Consumables are extra, capped at, um, eighteen hundred a year. Is that in the forty-four?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Honestly, I don't think so. I'd have to check.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay, that's one thing to pin down. I'll write it on my list.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Who do we ask?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Rui in procurement, probably. He handled the original.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can I jump in with something else? Sorry, the desk booking thing.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Go ahead, quickly.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: People in Leeds keep saying the booking screen shows desks free that are already taken. Hedda mentioned it twice.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Is that a facilities problem or an IT one?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Um, both? I'd say it's the sync, which is IT, but we get the angry emails.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Forward them on.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I did. Twice. Nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Put it in the ticket system and tag me, I'll nudge Daan.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: While we're on the Leeds office, did anyone sort the printer lease? It was due in March, I think.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: That's this month. Diego, you had that one.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yeah. Got two quotes. One's cheaper, one has toner included.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: What's the gap?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Couple hundred a year. Not much.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I'd rather have toner included then. Fewer little invoices.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Not decided though, right? You're just saying you'd prefer it.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right, just preferring. Send me the two numbers and we'll sort it by email.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Sorry, back on the cleaners for a moment. Is there anything else people want me to find out?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: A few things, yes. The consumables question, the log, and whether Bilal's team really uses it.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Okay, I'll write that down.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And I'd like to know what a competitor would charge. Even a rough figure. Otherwise forty-four is just a number somebody gave us.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I mean, I can ask around. I don't have any other names, though.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Ask Joao. He mentioned a firm in Manchester once.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Oh, I think maybe I remember. Is that, uh, Northgate something?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Think so. Not sure.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I'm wary of dragging this out. The fourteenth is close, and I don't want to go in blind and lose the rate lock.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Eleven days. We have time for a phone call.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: A call, sure. But a full tender in eleven days, no.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Nobody's suggesting a tender. Right?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: No, no. A ballpark.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Good. Because the bigger thing is the whole Leeds lease conversation, and that'll take everyone's attention soon.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Is that going ahead? I haven't heard anything since January.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I think there's a meeting. Hamid said something about a floor reduction.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Which would change the cleaning scope, wouldn't it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Exactly. Well, maybe. I don't know how much.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Oh. That would matter for a two year deal.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: It might. Or it might be nothing. I'll ask Hamid, though I'd bet he doesn't know either.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Ask anyway.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, so for the record, nothing's settled on the cleaners. The renewal is on the table, and we have homework.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll do the consumables and the competitor call.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: And I'll talk to Bilal and Hamid. Tomas, anything you want to take?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I'll pull the old invoices so we can see what we really paid last year. Maybe there are extras hiding in there.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good, thanks. That helps.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can we do the fire door thing now? I'm confused about who unlocks Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yes. Hedda said she'd be in at seven. She has the key.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And the alarm?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Rui has the code. Wait, no, it's Daan. Sorry, Daan.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: You sure?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Pretty sure. I'll double check and tell you tonight.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay. I have to go in two minutes, by the way. Call at half past.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine. Anything else, quickly? Elif, the quote, remember.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes, sending it right after.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Next time, same slot, same room. Thanks, all.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay, we're all here. Elif, the badge reader quote, did it land last week?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes. Um, I sent it Monday, I think. Maybe Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Found it, Tuesday. Second floor only, 2,350 fitted. So fifty over the line.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: That's close enough, right?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: It's close. I'll just absorb it.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Fitted meaning they do the cabling too?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: It says so. I'll confirm with them.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Mm. Worth confirming, cabling is where they get you.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Printer lease is signed. Toner one.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good. Thanks, Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Courier brings the unit Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Thursday is also the fire door contractor. Is that going to clash?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Different floors. Fine.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Marco, the cleaners. Did Rui get back to you on the consumables?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Not yet, no. I think maybe he's out until Wednesday? I sent it twice though.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine, that stays open. The rate lock is Friday the fourteenth, so we've got four days after this.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Right, right. I have it written down this time.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Elif, you said you'd chase a couple of other firms. Anything come back?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh, yes. So, two quotes came in on Friday, actually. I meant to forward them.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: One was a lot higher, we can ignore that one. The other is Kestrel Facilities, and they came in under, forty-one a year.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Forty-one thousand? Against forty-four?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yeah. And they put in credits if they miss a visit, and the contract can be left with ninety days' notice.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Credits how? A discount or an actual refund?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Um, off the next invoice. I'd have to reread it.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Send me the PDF after this.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes. And I rang three of their clients, they gave me names. None of them had missed a visit.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: None? Not one in how long?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: A year or more, for two of them. The third was newer. I didn't push on that.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: That's, well, that's quite good, I think.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Which kinds of clients? Offices?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Two offices and a clinic. Sorry, vague, I wrote it down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Put it in the notes when you send the PDF.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Kestrel. We should move to them.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Uh, shouldn't we, um, look at it a bit more first?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I mean, we've only just seen it. I think maybe-

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It's cheaper and it's got an exit.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Hang on, make the case properly. Cheaper by how much, once you net out everything?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Three grand a year, against the renewal.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Forty-four less forty-one, yes. Three thousand.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: And the exit's ninety days. If they're bad, we leave. Brightwash wants us in for two years. Kestrel does the handover with their own people, two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: That's fair. What about the changeover? Marco said three weeks of mess.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Like I said, two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Two weeks is still, you know, disruption.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Less than three.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, they could say two weeks and mean four.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Maybe. Then we use the exit.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. I'm hearing it, but we're not deciding it today. I haven't read the contract.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: No, of course. It's just the big picture, it looks promising.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Looks promising, agreed. Marco, can you get Brightwash to hold the rate lock a few more days?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I can ask. I think maybe they'd say no, though.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Ask anyway.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Okay. Today.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Also, what happened with Northgate? Did anyone call?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I think that was one of the quotes. Maybe the high one. I'd have to check the names.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Right, so you don't know either.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll check.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine. Moving on, because we have the recycling thing from the Leeds survey and I'd like to give it ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: The bins.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yes. Facilities got complaints about the sorting. Tomas, you had a view?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Um, yes. Get rid of the little bins at every desk. Put shared ones at each floor, by the kitchen and the printers.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Everyone would lose their own bin?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yes. Everyone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: People will grumble.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: They grumble at everything. Look at the numbers though. Cleaners spend thirty-five minutes a night going round the desk bins. A hundred and twenty of them.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Thirty-five minutes.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Every night. And on the pilot floor, the fourth, contamination in the recycling went from thirty-one percent down to twelve.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Thirty-one to twelve. That was the audit figure, from January?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yes, the one the waste contractor did.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: And the pilot floor is happy?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Mostly. One person asked for a bin back. Nobody else.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: What would it cost, to buy the shared ones?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Not much. I have a quote somewhere, a few hundred. I'd have to find it.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine, the cost doesn't change my mind. It's the cleaning minutes and the contamination. Go ahead and roll the shared floor bins out, and pull the desk ones.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Great. When?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Next month, floor by floor. Diego, can you co-ordinate with Hedda?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Do we tell people first?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: An email this week. Elif, can you draft that?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sure. Short and friendly.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good. Right, going back to the cleaners for one minute so nobody leaves confused.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Nothing's decided there.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Nothing's decided. Two options, Brightwash at forty-four and Kestrel at forty-one, and I'm going to read the Kestrel terms tonight.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: And I'll ask about the rate lock.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: And I'll send the PDF.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Anyone want to know my view again?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: We know it, Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I'd like Kestrel to answer a couple of questions in writing, though. Insurance, the key handling.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Write them down and send them to me, I'll pass them on.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Is it the same slot next week?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Same slot. Actually, Tuesday, I have something Monday.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Tuesday. Noted.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay, cleaners first today, because that one has a clock on it. Everybody here? Elif, you're on mute.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Good. So, I read the Kestrel contract last Tuesday night, all of it, and I have notes. Marco, where did you get to with Brightwash?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, so I asked about holding the rate. I think maybe they were annoyed, but they said they'd keep it until the end of this week.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Until Friday. Okay, that's something.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah. They said it's a one-off, though. I think they were quite clear about that.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: So four days.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Roughly, yes. Tuesday to Friday, if we count today as gone.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And the consumables? Did Rui ever come back?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: He did, Wednesday. So the forty-four doesn't include them. They're on top, up to the eighteen hundred cap, like Hana said.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: So really it's closer to forty-five eight if they use the whole cap.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I think so, yes. Maybe they wouldn't use all of it.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Last year's invoices, I pulled them. They billed about fourteen hundred in consumables. Bin liners, soap, the paper towels.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fourteen hundred. So call it forty-five and a half for Brightwash in practice.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Give or take. And Kestrel's forty-one, does that have supplies in it?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: That's my question for the Kestrel contract as well. Section six, I think. Let me find it.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Hurry up.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I'm looking, Diego. Okay. Consumables included, sorry, they say included, with a fair-use sentence I don't love.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: What's fair use mean when it's at home?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Doesn't say. I'd want a number in there.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Can I ask something a bit off-topic first? Is the lights thing on the third floor fixed? Hedda said the motion sensors are going on and off all day.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: That's Daan's, isn't it? I thought the electrician was in last week.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: He was, but it's apparently worse.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Worse how?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: People wave their arms to get the lights on. In meetings. That's what Hedda told me.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right. Put that in the ticket system and tag Daan, please. I'll mention it when I speak to him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Okay. Will do.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, back on the cleaners, sorry. Did Tomas's questions to Kestrel get answered? The insurance and the keys?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: They did, in writing, Thursday. Public liability is five million, certificate attached. I checked the expiry and it's good until next January.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: And keys?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Numbered keys, signed out, kept in a locked box at their depot, not with the cleaners. If one goes missing they pay for the lock change.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: That's more than Brightwash does.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Brightwash has the supervisor carry all of them around, I think. Which, frankly, is not great.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Is that, um, true? I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Joao told me once. Not sure how current it is.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Don't hang a conclusion on it. Joao's memory of something from a couple of years ago.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Fair.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: What I keep coming back to is, big picture, we have something that works and something that might work better. Isn't that the whole choice?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Pretty much, with the money on the side.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Kestrel's cheaper. Exit's ninety days.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I know your view, Diego.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Just saying.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: So let me go through the contract points I flagged, and then we should be able to get somewhere. First, the term. Initial period is twelve months, then rolling, and the ninety days can be used any time after month three.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Month three? Not from the start?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Not from the start, no. There's a settling-in period. So you can't walk away in the first ninety days.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Oh. So that's, um, six months really, before we're out in the worst case.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Roughly, yes. If we gave notice on day ninety-one, we'd be gone by about day one eighty.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Hang on, is that a problem? Because that's what Diego was selling as the safety net.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Still a safety net. Six months is not two years.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Six months of a bad cleaner is a long time.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Six months of a bad cleaner we'd be paying less for.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Ha. Fine.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Second, the credits. Missed visit, they credit one visit's worth against the next invoice. Not a refund. Elif, you asked about that, I think.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Right, I did say off the next invoice. Did I say that right?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Good. I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Third, the changeover. Two weeks, their own team does the walkthrough, we hand over the alarm codes on day one. They want a named contact on our side.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: That'd be me, I think. Or, well, someone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: We'll sort out who. Not the sticking point.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: What about the Brightwash notice period? Are we even allowed to leave at the end of this month?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Their current term ends the thirty-first. The renewal is optional, so we're fine. I checked that.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. Just checking, since people forget auto-renew clauses.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: There isn't one. That I did read.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Can I ask about the lease thing? Hamid, the floor reduction. Did he say anything?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I rang him Friday. He said the lease review is still going, nothing before the summer, and he doesn't expect a decision on the floors before the autumn.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: So it could shrink, but not soon.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Right. And that's a plus for the shorter commitment, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Because if the scope changes mid-contract with Brightwash we're stuck.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Well, we'd have to negotiate. With Kestrel we could leave.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I think maybe that's a good point. I hadn't thought about it that way.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Let me do the devil's advocate bit. Brightwash we know. Eleven complaints in twelve months, small ones. Kestrel we know from three phone calls.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Three of their clients, yes.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And one of them was fairly new. What do we really know about the new one?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I spoke to the contact again, actually. After the meeting. The newer one is a clinic and they've had them about five months, no missed visits.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Five months. Okay. That's better than I assumed.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I told you it was vague. It's in the notes now.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: It is. I read them.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: And Bilal? Did you find out if the complaints log is real?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I forgot to report that. Bilal says the office team still logs everything, and he thinks eleven is honest. If anything, a couple of items went in twice.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Then Brightwash's record is as good as it looked.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: As good as it looked, and no better.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: So it's decent. And Kestrel's cheaper.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, can I say something? I'm, I'm still a bit nervous about the three weeks of disruption. Even two.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I hear that. Joao's three weeks was his estimate for an unprepared handover. Kestrel's walkthrough is organised.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. I think maybe I'm just worried about the first week.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: The first week will be untidy whoever we pick. Not much we can do about it.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: We could put someone on site the first morning.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'll do that. I'm there Thursdays anyway.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: The start would be the first of April, not a Thursday, I think. Whatever. We'll find someone.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I'll swap.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Thanks. Okay, so the money. Brightwash at forty-four with the consumables on top, call it forty-five and a half. Kestrel at forty-one all in, once I get the fair-use wording tightened. That's, um, four and a half a year between them. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Over the first twelve months, anyway.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Over twelve, yes. Okay. I've read it, I've heard everyone, and I don't think more calls change much. Kestrel Facilities, then. We go with them for Leeds, and I'll ask for the supplies wording to be fixed before I sign anything.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Marco, can you let Brightwash know today, politely, and say thanks for holding the rate? I'll email Kestrel this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Um, yes. Sure. I think maybe I'll phone rather than email. It's, it's a bit awkward.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Phone is nicer. Keep it short.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Great, that's off the list then.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Ask them to name the supervisor in writing, as well. Whoever is on our floor.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: I'll put that in with the supplies wording.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Oh, one other thing, quickly. The recycling email, it went out Wednesday, and I've had eight replies already.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Eight. Complaints?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Mostly, yes. Two people want their bins back. Other six are, um, practical questions about batteries and coffee cups.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Fine, send the six practical ones to Diego, he's doing the rollout with Hedda.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Send them to me. I'll answer.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Okay. And the two?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Reply politely and tell them the pilot floor was fine. Don't argue.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I have to run to another call, I'm sorry, can I-

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Go, go. Phone Brightwash after.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Will do. Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Okay. Same slot next week, and I'll send the Kestrel paperwork round when I have it.
